_link.title: I can explain why forces perpendicular to displacement do no work

toLevel2.question: Which one of the following is the value of cos 90°?
toLevel2.correctExplanation: cos 90° = 0, which is why a force perpendicular to displacement produces zero work.

distractors.explanation: cos 0° = 1, not cos 90°. This value applies when force and displacement are aligned.
cos 180° = −1, not cos 90°. This value applies when the force opposes the displacement.
cos 60° = 0.5, not cos 90°. The cosine of 90° is exactly zero.

toLevel2.question: A constant force acts perpendicular to the direction of displacement of an object. Which one of the following is closest to the work done by the force on the object?
toLevel2.correctExplanation: W = Fs cos 90° = 0. A perpendicular force has no component in the direction of displacement.

distractors.answer: Maximum work
distractors.explanation: Maximum work occurs when the force is parallel to the displacement (θ = 0°), not perpendicular.

distractors.answer: Negative work
distractors.explanation: Negative work requires the force to oppose the displacement (90° < θ < 180°), not be perpendicular to it.

distractors.answer: Half the maximum work
distractors.explanation: Half the maximum work occurs at θ = 60° (cos 60° = 0.5), not at θ = 90°.

toLevel2.question: An object travels in uniform circular motion. Which one of the following best describes the net force acting on the object?
toLevel2.correct: A centripetal force directed toward the centre of the circular path
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The centripetal force always points toward the centre of the circular path, perpendicular to the velocity of the object.

distractors.answer: A force in the direction of the object's motion
distractors.explanation: In uniform circular motion there is no net force along the direction of motion; the net force is directed radially inward.

distractors.answer: No force acts on the object
distractors.explanation: A net force must act to change the direction of the velocity; this is the centripetal force.

distractors.answer: A centrifugal force directed outward from the centre
distractors.explanation: Centrifugal force is a fictitious force in rotating reference frames; the real net force is centripetal, directed inward.

toLevel2.question: An object travels in uniform circular motion. Which one of the following best describes why the kinetic energy of the object remains constant?
toLevel2.correct: The centripetal force is perpendicular to the velocity of the object
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Since the force is always perpendicular to the displacement, no work is done and the kinetic energy stays constant.

distractors.answer: There is no force acting on the object
distractors.explanation: A centripetal force acts continuously, but it does no work because it is perpendicular to the direction of motion.

distractors.answer: The speed of the object increases and decreases by equal amounts
distractors.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the speed is genuinely constant, not fluctuating.

distractors.answer: Energy is continuously supplied to the object
distractors.explanation: No energy input is required to maintain uniform circular motion in the absence of friction.

toLevel2.question: A waiter carries a tray of food horizontally across a room at constant speed. Which one of the following best describes the work done by the gravitational force on the tray?
toLevel2.correct: Zero, because the displacement is perpendicular to the gravitational force
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The gravitational force acts downward while the displacement is horizontal, making θ = 90° and the work equal to zero.

distractors.answer: Positive, because the waiter exerts an upward force on the tray
distractors.explanation: The upward support force balances the gravitational force but causes no vertical displacement, so no work is done.

distractors.answer: Positive, because the tray has mass and is moving
distractors.explanation: Having mass and moving does not guarantee work is done; the force must have a component along the displacement.

distractors.answer: It depends on the speed of the waiter
distractors.explanation: Speed does not affect whether work is done; what matters is the angle between the force and displacement.

toLevel2.question: A student claims: 'An object in uniform circular motion has constant kinetic energy because no work is done on it by the centripetal force.' The student's claim is correct.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The centripetal force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so W = Fs cos 90° = 0 and the kinetic energy stays constant.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: Students may think a force must change the energy of an object, but perpendicular forces change direction without changing speed or kinetic energy.

toLevel2.question: A student claims: 'A force can act on an object without doing any work on it.' The student's claim is correct.
toLevel2.correctExplanation: When a force is perpendicular to the displacement, the work done is zero even though a force is present.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: Students may assume all forces do work, but perpendicular forces transfer no energy.

toLevel2.prompt: Jo is studying the relationship between force direction and work. Complete the following statement about perpendicular forces.
toLevel2.sentence: When a force is perpendicular to the displacement, the work done is {{blank:1}} because cos 90° equals {{blank:2}}.

1.correctExplanation: W = Fs cos 90° = Fs × 0 = 0, so no energy is transferred.

distractors.answer: maximum
distractors.explanation: Maximum work occurs at θ = 0°, not 90°.

distractors.answer: negative
distractors.explanation: Negative work requires θ between 90° and 180°, not exactly 90°.

2.correctExplanation: The cosine of 90° is exactly zero, which makes the entire work calculation zero.

distractors.answer: one
distractors.explanation: cos 0° = 1, not cos 90°.

distractors.answer: negative one
distractors.explanation: cos 180° = −1, not cos 90°.

toLevel2.prompt: Sam is revising uniform circular motion. Complete the following statement about the centripetal force.
toLevel2.sentence: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal force is always {{blank:1}} to the velocity of the object.

1.correctExplanation: The centripetal force points toward the centre while the velocity is tangent to the circle, making them perpendicular.

distractors.answer: parallel
distractors.explanation: If the force were parallel to the velocity, the object would accelerate or decelerate along its path, not travel in a circle.

distractors.answer: opposite
distractors.explanation: An opposing force would decelerate the object along its path, not cause circular motion.

toLevel2.prompt: Kate is studying force components and work. Complete the following statement.
toLevel2.sentence: Only the component of force that is {{blank:1}} to the displacement can do work on an object.

1.correctExplanation: The parallel component (F cos θ) is the only part that transfers energy to or from the object.

distractors.answer: perpendicular
distractors.explanation: The perpendicular component changes the direction of motion but does not transfer energy.

distractors.answer: equal
distractors.explanation: The force does not need to equal the displacement; it must have a component along the displacement direction.

toLevel3.question: A satellite travels in a circular orbit around Earth. The gravitational force exerted on the satellite by Earth acts radially inward. Which one of the following best describes why the gravitational force does no work on the satellite?
toLevel3.correct: The gravitational force is always perpendicular to the displacement of the satellite
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The gravitational force points radially inward while the satellite moves tangentially, so the angle between them is always 90°.

distractors.answer: The gravitational force is too weak in space to do any work
distractors.explanation: The gravitational force is not weak; it provides the centripetal force. It does no work because of its perpendicular direction.

distractors.answer: The satellite has no mass in orbit
distractors.explanation: The satellite retains its mass in orbit; zero work is due to the force-displacement angle.

distractors.answer: The satellite moves too fast for the gravitational force to act
distractors.explanation: The gravitational force acts continuously on the satellite regardless of speed; it does no work because of the perpendicular geometry.

toLevel3.question: Anna swings a ball on a string in a horizontal circle at constant speed. Which one of the following best describes the work done by the tension in the string on the ball?
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The tension always points toward the centre while the ball moves tangentially, so the force is perpendicular to the displacement.

distractors.answer: Positive work equal to the kinetic energy of the ball
distractors.explanation: The tension maintains the circular motion but does not increase the kinetic energy of the ball.

distractors.answer: Negative work that decelerates the ball
distractors.explanation: The ball maintains constant speed because the tension does no work.

distractors.answer: Work equal to the tension multiplied by the circumference
distractors.explanation: This incorrectly assumes the force is parallel to the circular path.

toLevel3.question: Liam carries a heavy box across a level floor at constant speed. Which one of the following is closest to the work done by the gravitational force on the box?
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The gravitational force acts downward and the displacement is horizontal. The force is perpendicular to the displacement, so no work is done.

distractors.answer: Equal to the gravitational force multiplied by the distance walked
distractors.explanation: This would be true if the box were lifted vertically, but horizontal displacement is perpendicular to the gravitational force.

distractors.answer: Equal to the kinetic energy of the box
distractors.explanation: The kinetic energy relates to horizontal forces, not the vertical gravitational force.

distractors.answer: Equal to half the gravitational force multiplied by the distance
distractors.explanation: No fraction of the gravitational force does work when the displacement is entirely perpendicular to it.

toLevel3.question: An object travels in uniform circular motion under the action of a centripetal force. Which one of the following best describes the physical quantity that changes?
toLevel3.correct: The direction of the velocity of the object
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The centripetal force changes the direction of the velocity vector without changing its magnitude (speed).

distractors.answer: The speed of the object
distractors.explanation: In uniform circular motion, speed remains constant because the force is perpendicular to the velocity.

distractors.answer: The kinetic energy of the object
distractors.explanation: Kinetic energy depends on speed, which does not change in uniform circular motion.

distractors.answer: The mass of the object
distractors.explanation: Mass does not change due to forces acting on the object.

toLevel3.question: A charged particle moves through a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic force exerted on the particle is always perpendicular to the velocity of the particle. Which one of the following best describes the effect of the magnetic force?
toLevel3.correct: The particle changes direction but maintains constant speed
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A perpendicular force does no work, so the kinetic energy and speed are unchanged, but the direction of motion changes.

distractors.answer: The particle accelerates and gains kinetic energy
distractors.explanation: The perpendicular force cannot increase the kinetic energy; it only changes the direction of motion.

distractors.answer: The particle decelerates and eventually stops
distractors.explanation: The force does no work, so the particle cannot lose kinetic energy to the magnetic force.

distractors.answer: The particle moves in a straight line at higher speed
distractors.explanation: A perpendicular force curves the path rather than keeping it straight.

toLevel3.question: An object moves in a straight line while a constant force acts perpendicular to its direction of motion. Which one of the following best describes what happens to the speed of the object?
toLevel3.correct: The speed of the object remains constant
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A perpendicular force does zero work, so it cannot change the kinetic energy or speed of the object.

distractors.answer: The speed of the object increases gradually
distractors.explanation: A perpendicular force has no component along the direction of motion and cannot increase speed.

distractors.answer: The speed of the object decreases gradually
distractors.explanation: The force does no work and cannot remove kinetic energy from the object.

distractors.answer: The speed of the object fluctuates
distractors.explanation: The effect is predictable: zero work means constant kinetic energy and constant speed.

toLevel3.question: A student claims: 'The normal force exerted on a book by a horizontal table does zero work on the book as it slides across the table.' The student's claim is correct.
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The normal force acts vertically upward while the book moves horizontally, so the force is perpendicular to the displacement.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: Students may think the normal force contributes to the motion, but it is perpendicular to the horizontal displacement.

toLevel3.prompt: Ben is analysing the effect of a perpendicular force on an object's velocity. Complete the following statement.
toLevel3.sentence: A force perpendicular to the displacement changes the {{blank:1}} of an object's velocity without changing its {{blank:2}}.

1.correctExplanation: A perpendicular force deflects the object, changing its velocity direction.

distractors.answer: magnitude
distractors.explanation: The magnitude of velocity (speed) is unchanged by a perpendicular force.

distractors.answer: mass
distractors.explanation: Mass is not affected by applied forces.

2.correctExplanation: Since no work is done, the kinetic energy and speed remain constant.

distractors.answer: direction
distractors.explanation: Direction is exactly what changes when a perpendicular force acts.

distractors.answer: position
distractors.explanation: Position changes as the object moves; speed is what remains constant.

toLevel3.prompt: Anna is studying the forces on a box sliding across a horizontal surface. Complete the following statement about the normal force.
toLevel3.sentence: The normal force exerted on an object by a horizontal surface does {{blank:1}} work because it acts {{blank:2}} to the displacement.

1.correctExplanation: The normal force is vertical while the displacement is horizontal, giving W = Fs cos 90° = 0.

distractors.answer: positive
distractors.explanation: The normal force does not accelerate the object horizontally and does no work.

distractors.answer: negative
distractors.explanation: Negative work requires a force component opposing the displacement, which the normal force does not have.

2.correctExplanation: The normal force is vertical and the displacement is horizontal, making them perpendicular.

distractors.answer: parallel
distractors.explanation: Parallel would mean the force acts in the direction of motion, which the normal force does not.

distractors.answer: opposite
distractors.explanation: Opposite would mean the force opposes the motion; the normal force acts vertically, not horizontally.

toLevel3.prompt: Sam is revising uniform circular motion and energy. Complete the following statement.
toLevel3.sentence: In uniform circular motion, the kinetic energy remains {{blank:1}} because the centripetal force does no work.

1.correctExplanation: No work means no energy transfer, so the kinetic energy does not change.

distractors.answer: increasing
distractors.explanation: Kinetic energy would increase only if positive work were done on the object.

distractors.answer: decreasing
distractors.explanation: Kinetic energy would decrease only if negative work were done on the object.

toLevel4.question: A car travels at constant speed around a banked curve. The normal force exerted on the car by the road has both vertical and horizontal components. Which one of the following best describes the work done by the normal force on the car?
toLevel4.correct: Neither component does work if the speed is constant
toLevel4.correctExplanation: At constant speed on a banked curve, the net force is centripetal (perpendicular to the velocity), so no work is done and the kinetic energy is unchanged.

distractors.answer: The horizontal component does positive work
distractors.explanation: The horizontal component provides the centripetal force, which is perpendicular to the velocity of the car.

distractors.answer: The vertical component does negative work
distractors.explanation: The vertical component balances the gravitational force with no vertical displacement, so it does no work.

distractors.answer: Both components do equal amounts of work
distractors.explanation: Neither component does any work when the car maintains constant speed around the curve.

toLevel4.question: A satellite moves from point A to point B in its circular orbit. An engineer claims the gravitational force does work equal to mgh, where h is the altitude. Which one of the following best describes why this claim is incorrect?
toLevel4.correct: The displacement is tangential, not radial, so the gravitational force does no work
toLevel4.correctExplanation: In a circular orbit, the displacement is always perpendicular to the radial gravitational force, giving zero work at every point.

distractors.answer: The altitude does not change in a circular orbit
distractors.explanation: While the altitude is constant, the key reason is that the force and displacement are perpendicular.

distractors.answer: The gravitational force does not act beyond the atmosphere
distractors.explanation: The gravitational force acts on satellites; it provides the centripetal force for the orbit.

distractors.answer: Work should be calculated as mgh/2 in orbit
distractors.explanation: No fraction of mgh applies because the force is perpendicular to the displacement, giving zero work.

toLevel4.question: A pendulum swings from its highest point to its lowest point. Which one of the following best describes the work done by the tension in the string on the bob at the lowest point?
toLevel4.correct: Zero, because the tension is perpendicular to the velocity of the bob
toLevel4.correctExplanation: At every point in the swing, the tension acts along the string toward the pivot, perpendicular to the tangential velocity of the bob.

distractors.answer: Positive, because the tension accelerates the bob
distractors.explanation: The bob accelerates due to the tangential component of the gravitational force, not the tension. The tension is always perpendicular to the velocity.

distractors.answer: Negative, because the tension decelerates the bob
distractors.explanation: The tension is perpendicular to the path and cannot decelerate the bob; only the tangential component of the gravitational force does that.

distractors.answer: The tension does work only at the highest point
distractors.explanation: At all points of the swing, the tension is perpendicular to the velocity and does zero work.

toLevel4.question: A frictionless roller coaster car travels around a vertical loop. At the top of the loop, the normal force exerted on the car by the track points downward toward the centre. Which one of the following best describes the work done by the normal force at this point?
toLevel4.correct: Zero, because the normal force is perpendicular to the velocity of the car
toLevel4.correctExplanation: At the top of the loop, the car moves horizontally while the normal force points vertically downward, making them perpendicular.

distractors.answer: Positive, because the normal force pushes the car forward
distractors.explanation: The normal force points toward the centre of the loop, not along the direction of motion.

distractors.answer: Negative, because the normal force opposes the motion of the car
distractors.explanation: The normal force is centripetal and perpendicular to the velocity, not opposing it.

distractors.answer: Equal to the gravitational potential energy of the car
distractors.explanation: The normal force at any point in circular motion is perpendicular to the velocity and does zero work.

toLevel4.question: An ice skater glides in a straight line across frictionless ice. The gravitational force and the normal force act on the skater. Which one of the following is closest to the total work done by these two forces?
toLevel4.correctExplanation: Both the gravitational force (downward) and the normal force (upward) are perpendicular to the horizontal displacement, so neither does any work.

distractors.answer: Equal to the kinetic energy of the skater
distractors.explanation: The kinetic energy of the skater remains constant; these perpendicular forces do no work.

distractors.answer: Equal to mg multiplied by the distance travelled
distractors.explanation: This would apply if the skater moved vertically, but the displacement is horizontal and perpendicular to both forces.

distractors.answer: Negative, because the gravitational force pulls the skater downward
distractors.explanation: The gravitational force acts vertically but the displacement is horizontal, so no work is done.

toLevel4.question: A planet orbits a star in a perfectly circular orbit. Which one of the following is closest to the net work done by the gravitational force on the planet over one complete orbit?
toLevel4.correctExplanation: At every point in a circular orbit, the gravitational force is perpendicular to the velocity of the planet, so the instantaneous work is always zero.

distractors.answer: Equal to the orbital kinetic energy of the planet
distractors.explanation: Kinetic energy remains constant throughout a circular orbit because the gravitational force does no work.

distractors.answer: Equal to 2πr multiplied by the gravitational force
distractors.explanation: This assumes the force is parallel to the displacement around the orbit, but they are perpendicular.

distractors.answer: Positive during half the orbit and negative during the other half
distractors.explanation: This describes elliptical orbits, not circular orbits where the force and velocity are always perpendicular.

toLevel4.question: Kate swings a bucket of water in a vertical circle at constant speed. At the 3 o'clock position (side of the circle), which one of the following best describes the direction of the net force on the bucket?
toLevel4.correct: Horizontally toward the centre of the circle
toLevel4.correctExplanation: At the 3 o'clock position, the centripetal acceleration points horizontally toward the centre, perpendicular to the upward or downward velocity.

distractors.answer: Vertically downward due to the gravitational force only
distractors.explanation: The gravitational force acts downward, but the tension also acts, and the net force must point toward the centre for circular motion.

distractors.answer: Tangent to the circle in the direction of motion
distractors.explanation: At constant speed, there is no tangential net force; the net force is centripetal.

distractors.answer: Vertically upward opposing the gravitational force on the bucket
distractors.explanation: The net force must point toward the centre of the circle, not simply upward.

toLevel4.prompt: Liam is analysing the forces on a pendulum bob. Complete the following statement.
toLevel4.sentence: The tension in a pendulum string does no work on the bob because the tension is always {{blank:1}} to the velocity of the bob along the arc.

1.correctExplanation: The tension acts along the string toward the pivot, which is always at 90° to the tangential velocity.

distractors.answer: parallel
distractors.explanation: If the tension were parallel to the velocity, it would do work and change the speed of the bob directly.

distractors.answer: opposite
distractors.explanation: The tension points toward the pivot, not opposite to the direction of swing.

toLevel4.prompt: Jo is studying a satellite in circular orbit. Complete the following statement about the forces on the satellite.
toLevel4.sentence: A satellite in circular orbit maintains constant speed because the gravitational force is {{blank:1}} to the direction of {{blank:2}}.

1.correctExplanation: The gravitational force points radially inward while the satellite moves tangentially, making them perpendicular.

distractors.answer: parallel
distractors.explanation: The gravitational force is radial and the velocity is tangential; they are perpendicular in circular orbit.

distractors.answer: opposite
distractors.explanation: The gravitational force does not act opposite to the velocity of the satellite in circular orbit.

2.correctExplanation: The direction of motion of the satellite is tangent to the orbit, perpendicular to the radial gravitational force.

distractors.answer: gravity
distractors.explanation: This would make the sentence say gravity is perpendicular to gravity, which is circular.

distractors.answer: acceleration
distractors.explanation: The acceleration is centripetal and parallel to the gravitational force, not perpendicular to it.

toLevel4.prompt: Ben is studying the normal force on a flat surface. Complete the following statement.
toLevel4.sentence: On a flat surface, the normal force never does work because there is no {{blank:1}} displacement.

1.correctExplanation: The normal force is vertical, so it requires vertical displacement to do work, which does not occur on a flat surface.

distractors.answer: horizontal
distractors.explanation: There is horizontal displacement on a flat surface; the normal force is vertical and perpendicular to it.

distractors.answer: angular
distractors.explanation: Angular displacement is relevant to rotational motion, not the linear work done by the normal force.

toLevel5.question: A spacecraft uses a gravitational slingshot around a planet in a hyperbolic trajectory. Unlike circular orbits, the spacecraft gains speed. Which one of the following best describes how this relates to the perpendicular force principle?
toLevel5.correct: The trajectory is not circular, so the gravitational force is not always perpendicular to the velocity
toLevel5.correctExplanation: In a non-circular trajectory, the gravitational force has a component along the velocity direction at most points, allowing it to do work and change the speed.

distractors.answer: The gravitational force becomes stronger near the planet and does more work
distractors.explanation: While the gravitational force is stronger closer to the planet, the key point is that the force is no longer perpendicular to the velocity in non-circular paths.

distractors.answer: The motion of the planet adds energy that violates the perpendicular principle
distractors.explanation: The motion of the planet does transfer energy, but the fundamental point is that the force is not perpendicular in a slingshot trajectory.

distractors.answer: The perpendicular force principle does not apply in space
distractors.explanation: The principle applies everywhere; it is the trajectory shape that determines whether the force is perpendicular.

toLevel5.question: Anna swings a ball as a conical pendulum in a horizontal circle at constant speed. The tension in the string has both vertical and horizontal components. Which one of the following best describes the work done by the tension on the ball?
toLevel5.correct: Neither component does work on the ball
toLevel5.correctExplanation: The vertical component balances the gravitational force with no vertical displacement, and the horizontal component provides the centripetal force perpendicular to the horizontal velocity.

distractors.answer: The horizontal component does positive work
distractors.explanation: The horizontal component is centripetal, pointing toward the centre and perpendicular to the tangential velocity.

distractors.answer: The vertical component does negative work
distractors.explanation: The vertical component supports the ball against the gravitational force, but there is no vertical displacement.

distractors.answer: Both components do work that cancels out
distractors.explanation: Neither component does any work; this is not a case of cancellation.

toLevel5.question: An electron spirals in a magnetic field. The magnetic force exerted on the electron is always perpendicular to the velocity of the electron. The electron then also passes through an electric field parallel to its velocity. Which one of the following best describes what changes?
toLevel5.correct: The electric field does work on the electron, changing its speed
toLevel5.correctExplanation: The electric force parallel to the velocity has a component along the displacement and therefore does work, unlike the perpendicular magnetic force.

distractors.answer: Both fields now do work on the electron equally
distractors.explanation: The magnetic force remains perpendicular to the velocity and still does no work regardless of the electric field.

distractors.answer: The electric field also does no work on the electron
distractors.explanation: A force parallel to the velocity is not perpendicular and therefore does do work.

distractors.answer: The magnetic force starts doing work due to the electric field
distractors.explanation: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity by definition and never does work.

toLevel5.question: A cyclist rides at constant speed around a velodrome (banked circular track). Ignore air resistance and friction losses. Which one of the following best describes the work done by the normal force exerted on the cyclist by the banked surface?
toLevel5.correctExplanation: The normal force is perpendicular to the track surface and to the velocity of the cyclist. At constant speed, no net work is done.

distractors.answer: Positive work equal to the centripetal energy
distractors.explanation: There is no concept of 'centripetal energy'; the centripetal force is perpendicular to the velocity and does no work.

distractors.answer: Negative work opposing the motion of the cyclist
distractors.explanation: The normal force is perpendicular to the velocity and does not oppose or assist the motion.

distractors.answer: Work equal to mgs where s is the distance
distractors.explanation: This expression applies when the force is parallel to the displacement; the normal force is perpendicular.

toLevel5.question: A Ferris wheel rotates at constant angular speed. At the top, the gravitational force points downward and the passenger moves horizontally. At the side, the passenger moves vertically. Which one of the following is closest to the net work done by the gravitational force on a passenger over one full revolution?
toLevel5.correctExplanation: Over a complete revolution, the passenger returns to the same height, so the net vertical displacement is zero and the gravitational force does zero net work.

distractors.answer: Positive, because the gravitational force accelerates the passenger on the way down
distractors.explanation: While the gravitational force does positive work on the descent, it does equal negative work on the ascent, giving zero net work over a full revolution.

distractors.answer: Negative, because the motor must work against the gravitational force
distractors.explanation: The motor does work, but the gravitational force itself does zero net work over a complete revolution.

distractors.answer: Equal to mg multiplied by the circumference of the wheel
distractors.explanation: This treats the gravitational force as if it were always parallel to the displacement, but the angle varies continuously.

toLevel5.question: A hammer thrower spins a 7.26 kg hammer in a horizontal circle, gradually increasing its speed before release. Which one of the following best describes the forces required during the acceleration phase?
toLevel5.correct: A tangential force must also act in addition to the centripetal force to increase the speed
toLevel5.correctExplanation: The centripetal force is perpendicular to the velocity and cannot change the speed. A tangential force component parallel to the velocity must do work to increase the kinetic energy.

distractors.answer: The centripetal force alone increases both the speed and changes the direction
distractors.explanation: The centripetal force can only change direction; it cannot increase speed because it is perpendicular to the velocity.

distractors.answer: The centripetal force changes to become tangential during acceleration
distractors.explanation: The centripetal force always points toward the centre; a separate tangential force must act.

distractors.answer: No force is needed because the hammer naturally accelerates
distractors.explanation: Speed increases only when a net force component acts along the direction of motion.

toLevel5.question: In a particle accelerator, charged particles travel in circular paths using magnetic fields. Which one of the following best describes why electric fields, not magnetic fields, are used to accelerate the particles?
toLevel5.correct: Magnetic forces are perpendicular to the velocity and cannot do work
toLevel5.correctExplanation: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity of the particle, so it changes the direction of motion but cannot increase the kinetic energy. Electric fields can act parallel to the velocity.

distractors.answer: Magnetic fields are too weak to accelerate particles
distractors.explanation: Magnetic fields can be very strong; the issue is the direction of the force, not its magnitude.

distractors.answer: Electric fields are perpendicular while magnetic fields are parallel
distractors.explanation: This reverses the actual situation; the magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity.

distractors.answer: Both can accelerate particles equally but electric fields are less expensive
distractors.explanation: The distinction is physical, not economic; magnetic forces fundamentally cannot do work.

toLevel5.question: An amusement park ride spins passengers in a vertical circle at constant speed. At which position(s) does the gravitational force do zero instantaneous work on a passenger?
toLevel5.correct: At the very top and very bottom of the circle
toLevel5.correctExplanation: At the top and bottom, the velocity is horizontal while the gravitational force is vertical, making them perpendicular and giving zero instantaneous work.

distractors.answer: At the sides of the circle (3 and 9 o'clock positions)
distractors.explanation: At the sides, the velocity has a vertical component parallel to the gravitational force, so the gravitational force does non-zero work.

distractors.answer: The gravitational force does zero work at all positions in the circle
distractors.explanation: This is only true for a horizontal circle; in a vertical circle, the gravitational force does work at most positions.

distractors.answer: The gravitational force never does zero work during the rotation
distractors.explanation: At the top and bottom, the gravitational force is perpendicular to the horizontal velocity, giving zero work at those instants.

toLevel5.prompt: Liam is analysing the forces required to change the speed of an object in circular motion. Complete the following statement.
toLevel5.sentence: To increase the speed of an object in circular motion, a force component {{blank:1}} to the velocity must act, because the centripetal force is {{blank:2}} to the velocity and cannot change the speed.

1.correctExplanation: A parallel force component does positive work, increasing the kinetic energy and speed.

distractors.answer: perpendicular
distractors.explanation: A perpendicular force changes direction only and cannot increase speed.

distractors.answer: equal
distractors.explanation: The force need not equal the velocity; it must have a component along the velocity direction.

2.correctExplanation: The centripetal force always points toward the centre, perpendicular to the tangential velocity.

distractors.answer: parallel
distractors.explanation: If the centripetal force were parallel to the velocity, it would change the speed rather than the direction.

distractors.answer: opposite
distractors.explanation: The centripetal force is inward and perpendicular, not opposite to the direction of motion.

toLevel5.prompt: Kate is studying particle accelerators. Complete the following statement about the role of magnetic and electric fields.
toLevel5.sentence: In a particle accelerator, {{blank:1}} fields steer particles in circles while {{blank:2}} fields accelerate them, because only forces with a component along the velocity can do work.

1.correctExplanation: Magnetic forces are always perpendicular to the velocity, so they change the direction of motion without changing the speed.

distractors.answer: electric
distractors.explanation: Electric fields can act parallel to the velocity and are used for acceleration, not steering.

distractors.answer: gravitational
distractors.explanation: Gravitational fields are negligible for charged particle control in accelerators.

2.correctExplanation: Electric fields can exert force parallel to the velocity, doing work and increasing the kinetic energy.

distractors.answer: magnetic
distractors.explanation: Magnetic forces are perpendicular to the velocity and cannot accelerate particles.

distractors.answer: nuclear
distractors.explanation: Nuclear forces act at subatomic distances and are not used for bulk particle acceleration.
